heritage.p1: The gate towers are bjov: Vainakh combat towers that Chechen and Ingush clans built in the Caucasus from the 11th to 18th centuries.
heritage.p2: Builders stacked dressed stone without mortar. They kept the base heavy, narrowed the shaft, and crowned the roof with a pointed tsurko.
heritage.p3: I use them as a bridge: Caucasus roots, Norwegian life, two mountain cultures that respect endurance and craft.

facts.v: Combat tower. 20-25 m, four to five floors, square footprint.
Pointed stone crowning the stepped pyramid roof.
Stone overhangs. Defenders used them to protect the tower from above.
Proud stone. A dressed keystone above doors and windows, often carved with the owner’s name.
Residential tower. Families lived around a hearth and the central pillar, Aerd-Bogham.

heritage.title: Bjov: the combat tower, surveyed
heritage.body: Vainakh clans stacked dressed stone without mortar, heavy at the foot, narrow at the top. My roots are in the Caucasus and my life is in Norway — two mountain cultures with the same habit of building for weather.

hero.lede: Full-stack developer and designer in Norway. I build web apps from the database to the interface. The latest, Loyvetmitt, turns one Excel file of shifts into each driver's pay.

bio: I'm a developer and designer with roots in the Caucasus. At <mash>Mash Partners</mash> I take every site from the first sketch to the finished code, and <loyvetmitt>Loyvetmitt</loyvetmitt> was made the same way.
I'm doing a master's in informatics at NTNU and a bachelor's in accounting at UINN, and I've had <background>a job alongside school</background> since 2020.
